Ukraine’s Drone Offensive Gives Kyiv a 3-to-1 Edge Over Russia

Major Ukrainian attacks have frequently involved hundreds, and at times more than a thousand, drones directed at military, industrial, and energy targets across Russia. By contrast, Russian strikes have generally relied on smaller numbers of drones supplemented by missiles. Even so, Ukraine appears to be launching several times more long-range strike drones at targets inside Russia than Moscow is sending in the opposite direction.

corpus.title: Russian Strikes On Ukraine As Zelenskyy Says Russia Not Ready To End War
corpus.signal_text:
Russian drone strikes killed at least four people in Ukraine overnight and into September 27, including one person in the capital, Kyiv, and three in the southeastern Zaporizhzhya region, Ukrainian officials said.
In Kyiv, a man was killed when a Russian drone struck a nonresidential building in the Solomyansky district, Ukraine's State Emergency Service said.
A fire broke out at a car-repair facility in the same district, while another nonresidential building was hit, the agency said.
It shared images showing firefighters battling fires at the damaged buildings.
Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko said a Russian strike on the Shevchenkivsky district injured a woman and two 16-year-old children. The three were hospitalized, he said.
In the Zaporizhzhya region in the country's southeast , three people were killed in Russian strikes, according to the regional military administration.
A man was killed in the village of Komyshuvakha, where one house was destroyed and several others damaged, it said. Two more people, a man and a woman, were killed when a Russian strike hit their car in the village of Novotavriyske.
Four people were also wounded in the attack on Komyshuvakha, the administration said.
Trump Tells Kyiv To 'Settle' War
Meanwhile, US President Donald Trump has declined to confirm that he had agreed to allow Ukraine to produce Patriot missiles, despite Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy's statement on September 25 that Trump had made a “final decision” to grant Kyiv a license to produce the air-defense missiles.
Asked about the Patriot agreement on September 26, Trump said he wanted Zelenskyy and Russian President Vladimir Putin to “settle” their war.
Trump and Zelenskyy met on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly in New York on September 22.
“We talked about a lot of different subjects, and many of those subjects...very strong agreement,” Trump told reporters about the meeting.
“But you know what I want him to do? Make a deal. I want him to settle with Putin, and I want Putin to settle with him.”
Zelenskyy said after the meeting that he hoped Washington would help end the war “as soon as possible.” He has also called on Trump to maintain pressure on Moscow, including through new sanctions.
Zelenskyy: Putin Seeks Excuses To Keep Fighting
In his latest nightly video address, Zelenskyy said Moscow is showing no signs it is ready to end its war on its neighbor and he called on the West to remain united in efforts to force the Kremlin to the negotiating

Russian attack on Vyshneve in Kyiv region kills one and injures three others
Ukrinform
    In Vyshneve, Kyiv region, on September 27, one person was killed and three others were injured as a result of a Russian attack.
    According to Ukrinform, Timur Tkachenko, head of the Kyiv Regional State Administration, reported this on Telegram.
In Vyshneve, five vehicles were damaged when an enemy UAV struck. A fire broke out.
The condition of the injured is being assessed. They are receiving all necessary medical care.
In Brovary, the attack caused fires in a warehouse and an office building. No one was injured.
According to Tkachenko, rescue workers and all necessary services are on the scene, dealing with the aftermath of the attack.
As reported by Ukrinform, over the past 24 hours, 16 facilities in the Bucha, Fastiv, and Brovary districts of the Kyiv region were damaged by Russian drone attacks.
